title: Area of a circle
goal: I can calculate the area of a circle and of parts of circles.
teach: The area of a circle is A = π × r² (radius squared, then times π). If you know the diameter, halve it first. A semicircle has half the area of the full circle. A ring is the big circle minus the small circle.
tvis: A = 3,14 × 10² = 314 cm²

ex.q: Find the area of a ring with outer radius 10 cm and inner radius 5 cm.
steps: A = π × r². Big circle: A = 3,14 × 10² = 3,14 × 100 = 314 cm².

watch:
Square the radius, not the diameter: for d = 10, use r = 5.

Problem-solving lens
Write r = … first, even when the question gives the diameter.
